Job Description
Weapons Delivery System Technicians are responsible for operation, maintenance, and repair of weapons systems, which include Vertical Launching
Systems (VLS), major/minor caliber gun weapons systems, and Surface Vessel Torpedo Tubes (SVTT); conduct mechanical, electrical, and electronic
casualty analyses using technical publications, electronic/hydraulic schematics, circuit diagrams, and blueprints; repair, maintain, test, and calibrate
ordnance equipment; service and repair hydraulic and pneumatic systems; and maintain and repair magazine sprinkler, fire suppression, and deluge systems.

common_text: Gunner's Mates (GM) operate, perform, and coordinate organizational and intermediate maintenance on guided missile launching systems, gun weapons systems, gun mounts, small arms, torpedoes, and associated handling equipment; make detailed electrical, electronic, hydraulic, and mechanical casualty analyses; inspect, test, analyze, and direct repair of electric, electronic, hydraulic, mechanical, and servo systems; test and inspect ammunition, missiles, and their components; prepare torpedoes and torpedo launching equipment for storage, issue, and firing; prepare missiles and launching equipment for storage, issue, and firing; prepare gun weapons systems for firing; test, inspect, and repair magazine sprinkler and fire suppression systems; supervise personnel in handling and stowing of ammunition, missiles, and their components; inspect and direct repair of magazines and ammunition stowage spaces; inspect and repair ordnance and weapons handling equipment; supervise crews assigned to ordnance equipment; lead the command explosive safety programs; prepare global end-to- end management, storage, transport, and distribution of Arms Ammunition and Explosives (AA&E); and train and supervise personnel in small arms qualifications and Anti-Terrorism Force Protection (ATFP). __________________________________________

Gunner's Mates (GM) operate, perform, and coordinate organizational and intermediate maintenance on guided missile launching systems, gun weapons systems, gun mounts, small arms, torpedoes, and associated handling equipment; make detailed electrical, electronic, hydraulic, and mechanical casualty analyses; inspect, test, analyze, and direct repair of electric, electronic, hydraulic, mechanical, and servo systems; test and inspect ammunition, missiles, and their components; prepare torpedoes and torpedo launching equipment for storage, issue, and firing; prepare missiles and launching equipment for storage, issue, and firing; prepare gun weapons systems for firing; test, inspect, and repair magazine sprinkler and fire suppression systems; supervise personnel in handling and stowing of ammunition, missiles, and their components; inspect and direct repair of magazines and ammunition stowage spaces; inspect and repair ordnance and weapons handling equipment; supervise crews assigned to ordnance equipment; lead the command explosive safety programs; prepare global end-to- end management, storage, transport, and distribution of Arms Ammunition and Explosives (AA&E); and train and supervise personnel in small arms qualifications and Anti-Terrorism Force Protection (ATFP). __________________________________________

Weapons Delivery System Technicians are responsible for operation, maintenance, and repair of weapons systems, which include Vertical Launching Systems (VLS), major/minor caliber gun weapons systems, and Surface Vessel Torpedo Tubes (SVTT); conduct mechanical, electrical, and electronic casualty analyses using technical publications, electronic/hydraulic schematics, circuit diagrams, and blueprints; repair, maintain, test, and calibrate ordnance equipment; service and repair hydraulic and pneumatic systems; and maintain and repair magazine sprinkler, fire suppression, and deluge systems.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
